full_judgment:
7. Mr. Chowdhury submitted that there was delay in lodging the F.I.R., giving a chance of false implication of the appellants who have admitted enmity with the informant party. Alleged time .and place of occurrence could not be satisfactorily proved by the prosecution. All the witnesses are close relations of the informant and enmical to the accused appellants and no disinterested and independent witness was examined to support the prosecution case. Some of the charge-sheet witnesses were withheld giving rise to adverse presumption against the prosecution. He further submit-ted that examination of the accused appellants, especially appellant Hafez Munshi under Section 342 Cr.P.C. was defective. In support of his submissions the learned Advocate relied on some decisions and we shall revert to the same while dealing with the said submissions. 

 14. Learned Advocate for the appellant strenuously argued that non-production of those seizure list witnesses seriously affected the defence in as much as those witnesses, if produced, would not have supported the prosecution case and could have supported the defence version of the case. He, therefore, submitted that their non-production will raise an adverse presumption against the prosecution under Section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. Prosecution submitted two applications after examinations of P.Ws. 1-11 were concluded on 7.6.88 praying for exempting the production of Siraj Munshi, Hatem Howlader, Majid Munshi, A. Rob Sk. and Moslem Munshi on the ground that they were gained over by the accused party and prayed for issuing warrant of arrest on the remaining witnesses. The said application for exemption was signed, by the informant A. Rob himself. The Court, after hearing, by order dated 7.6.88, allowed the prayer for exemption of the said 5 witnesses and also the prayer for issuing warrant of arrest against the remaining charge-sheet witnesses. Thereafter, remaining P.Ws. 12, 13 and 14 were examined. Charge-sheet witnesses Daliluddin Munshi and Constable No. 91 Mofazzal Hossain could not be examined. Constable Mofazzal Hossain is a formal witness. He along with another constable P.W.13 Shamsul Huq took the dead body of the victim to the morgue. Daliluddin Munshi as already noticed; is an attesting witness of seizure list Ext. 13. He is cousin of the informant and maternal uncle of accused Soleman and also a resident of the same house with the informant. Moreover, C.S. witness Moslem is a distant cousin of the victim, C.S. witness Siraj is cousin of the informant residing in the same house, C.S. witness A. Rob Sk. is Mamato Bhai of the victim and C.S. witness A. Majid is the distant cousin of the informant residing in the same house. From the facts and circumstances discussed above, we are of the view that non-examination of those witnesses is not fatal to the prosecution case. They being the relations of both the parties were reluctant to depose in the case and prosecution tried its level best to examine them but failed in its effort to examine them.
